{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash
# Flux batch script converted from Slurm

# NOTE: Run with: flux batch <this_script>

# Slurm resources:
#   -p RM
#   -t 48:00:00
#   -N 8
#   --ntasks-per-node 26   (total tasks = 208)
#   -A phy210030p
#   --mail-type=BEGIN,END,FAIL
#   --mail-user=akshay2
#   --output=/ocean/projects/phy210030p/akshay2/Slurm_logs/multi_acceljerk_%j.log

#flux: -N 8
#flux: -n 208
#flux: -c 1
#flux: --time-limit=48h

# Omitted Slurm option: -p RM (partition)
# Flux queues/partitions are site-specific; no portable equivalent.
# Performance implication: job may run with different limits/priority or be rejected by policy.

# Omitted Slurm option: -A phy210030p (account)
# Flux accounting/project selection is site-specific; no portable equivalent.
# Performance implication: job may be charged to a default account or be rejected by policy.

# Omitted Slurm options: --mail-type and --mail-user
# Flux does not provide a universal, built-in email notification directive in batch scripts.
# Performance implication: none on runtime performance, but you will not receive automatic job emails.

# Omitted Slurm option: --output=... with %j token
# Slurm's %j token (job id) is not portable in Flux output directives.
# Performance implication: none, but log naming may differ unless you set a fixed filename.

module load openmpi/3.1.6-gcc8.3.1

CMDDIR=$PROJECT/HPC_pulsar/cmd_files

echo "Requested tasks: 208"

# If the .cmd file expects to launch MPI ranks itself, running it directly is fine.
# If it expects the scheduler to launch ranks, use flux-run.
flux run -n 208 -c 1 $CMDDIR/multinode_accelsearch.cmd
"
}
